summary:
Orbit shift is a browser-based 3D game where young astronauts (ages 7–12) run a lunar and Martian outpost. Players register as a junior astronaut and begin on the Moon, landing near the real Apollo 12 site on a terrain model built from actual lunar elevation data. They manage altitude, descent speed and fuel to touch down on the target zone, then spend limited points to build the outpost. A first-person walk-around mode lets them explore, pick up and use items, and progress sol by sol. Earning the Moon badge gives the chance to get the mission to Mars.

The game addresses the challenge by turning real engineering trade-offs, such as fuel, building priorities and limited resources, into hands-on decisions with visible consequences, rather than oversimplified facts or overly technical content. Age and region options, friendly instructions, sound and tablet touch controls make it accessible to children around the world.

It matters because children learn best by doing. Experiencing how one choice can make a mission succeed or fail builds systems thinking, problem-solving and curiosity, helping inspire the next generation of space explorers also solving the problem where some games dont attract the children's attention or even do't teach them anything
details: Our project is called ORBIT SHIFT .Orbit shift is a game designed to help kids with age ranging from 7 to 12 years where they get an astronaut experience from their missions on the moon and on other planets . It is an interactive open world game that consists of exploring the space and trying to survive on the planets responding to daily challenges inspired by the one real astronauts meet with when in space . It is fun, interactive and educating at the same time. Our intended impact is that children learn about life in space and challenges . 3D resources, Java script ,Python ,Artificial Intelligence and computers, were used while developing this project. In our project , real life challenges like descicion making , dilemmas and consequences of actions taken. Simplicity , age limits , and interactions .
